sites.name: de Gerlache rim ridge
sites.summary: A well-lit ridge on the rim of de Gerlache crater, about 16 km from the named feature of NASA's de Gerlache Rim 2 candidate region.
processes: Cold trapping of volatiles in permanent shadow
limits: Earth's gravity is about 6 times the Moon's
The Moon has no atmosphere; Earth sites cannot reproduce vacuum
Permanently shadowed lunar craters reach far colder temperatures than anywhere on Earth

criteria.label: Sunlit time
criteria.rule: >= 50 % at the surface (ours; published 85-95 % is 2-10 m above ground)

selection.note: Passes all four criteria; among the best-lit spots at the pole. It sits next to NASA's de Gerlache Rim 2 region (16.1 km from its named feature), which cross-checks our method against NASA's own choice.

sites.name: Shackleton-de Gerlache connecting ridge
sites.summary: The ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters, already known in the literature as one of the best-lit places at the south pole. Our screening found it independently.

sites.name: Cabeus-Malapert ridge
sites.summary: A ridge between the rim of Cabeus crater and Mons Malapert, outside NASA's candidate regions. Cabeus is where NASA's LCROSS impact found water ice in 2009; this spot is the best lit of our lunar candidates and keeps Earth in view most of the time.

selection.note: Passes all four criteria, 42 km from the nearest NASA Artemis feature: a proposal outside NASA's regions, inside the polar lighting zone (south of 84 S) and at least as well lit as our candidates next to NASA's regions.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3
sites.summary: India's 2023 lander, one of the landings closest to the lunar south pole, on old highland terrain lit by a low Sun.
limits: Earth's gravity is about 6 times the Moon's
The Moon has no atmosphere; Earth sites cannot reproduce vacuum
Surface radiation on the Moon is far higher

criteria.label: Sunlit time
criteria.rule: >= 50 % at the surface (ours; published 85-95 % is 2-10 m above ground)

criteria.label: Distance to permanent shadow
criteria.rule: <= 10 km (ours) — no permanent shadow found within ~29 km

selection.note: A good landing site — flat and always in view of Earth — but a normal day/night cycle and no permanent shadow nearby: fine for a short mission, not for a permanent base.

sites.name: Southern Elysium Planitia
sites.summary: A wide, low, flat plain in southern Elysium Planitia, about 220 km from Avernus Colles. The most interior point of the largest safe area on Mars.
limits: Earth's gravity is about 2.6 times Mars gravity
Mars air is about 100 times thinner and mostly CO2
Surface radiation on Mars is far higher

criteria.label: Air to slow down (est. surface pressure)
Slope at ~4 km scale
criteria.rule: <= 2.0 deg (ours, ~3x the past landings except Curiosity)

criteria.label: Relief over ~18 km
criteria.rule: <= 500 m (ours, ~2x the past landings except Curiosity)

selection.note: Passes every criterion inside a 4330 thousand km2 safe area, 220 km from its edge, and more than 500 km from any past landing. Second look at 463 m: 95 % of slopes below 1.05 deg, relief 50 m over 25 km (landings for comparison: InSight 0.53 deg / 90 m, Viking 1 0.94 deg / 72 m, Spirit 1.49 deg / 297 m).
